chapter: Recent years and early piano influences
title: Tatum's hands
summary: Wide palm, short strong stubby fingers, thumb on white keys; palm and finger length compared.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: What sort of hands had he got?

He had a wide palm with short fingers. Short fingers. It looked that way. Actually, his fingers were very strong. Apparently, he must have practiced...he must have been a very dedicated pianist. The way he spread his whole ten fingers on the piano like that, just like he was just laying his hands, but all the sensitivity in it... The balls of his fingers were very sensitive, and... His hand
had stubby fingers, kind of stubby fingers.
Gee, they didn't look very large. But he just made a tenth; he made a tenth... He had his own technique and his thumb...
Willie Smith had got quite long fingers...
His thumb was restricted to the white keys, his thumb always played the white keys, but he had a certain agility in his thumb that would... All of his fingers just seemed to work the same way.
But this isn't the hands. Now, your fingers were long, but your palm isn't as broad. Is that where...

Yeah, his palm... He had a good-sized palm length. That has to do with the sonority of your playing, I think. If you have a solid palm, I think that's instrumental in getting a big...a fairly good, round sound out of a piano. I mean, if you have thin fingers or something like that, you just have to work on it. You know, some people are able...lay their hands on the piano, just naturally they have the ability to get around the keyboard, you know. Some of them don't know what to do with it, but...
Well, I never really thought of that before, but... So that actually, if your fingers were a bit shorter but you
had a wider palm, it almost equals having long palms and a narrow palm.
